verdict: ServiceNow grew revenue 22% to $3.77B and pushed future booked revenue to $27.7B, though $547M of stock pay kept GAAP profit to $469M.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: Companies paying to use the ServiceNow platform — 97% of all revenue; grew 22% YoY (19% in constant currency).

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Consultants who help customers set the platform up.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to big companies — the largest running cost.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI features.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

otherDetail: Interest income of $88M plus other income, net of $82M — a net $170M gain outside operations.
oneTimers: Stock-based compensation was $547M in the quarter (including $96M inside cost of revenues) — the main reason non-GAAP net income ($1,012M) is more than double the GAAP figure ($469M). The cost is real; it is paid in shares instead of cash.
ServiceNow closed its Armis acquisition early in the quarter, expanding its security business; the company raised its full-year subscription revenue outlook in this release.
footerNote: ServiceNow raised its FY26 subscription revenue outlook in this release.

takeaways.title: Growth held up
takeaways.text: Total revenue grew 22% to $3.77B and subscription revenue 22% — ServiceNow beat the high end of its guidance and raised its full-year subscription outlook.

takeaways.title: Future revenue is booked
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — revenue customers have signed for but not yet been billed as sales — grew 25% to $27.7B, with $12.64B due in the next 12 months.

takeaways.title: Two very different profits
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.45 against $0.97 non-GAAP: $547M of stock-based compensation is the biggest single difference between the two profit pictures.

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to cents, so the waterfall lands a cent above the $12.44 kept as profit.
